_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Mathematics Standard (041), 2024, set 30/3/3 (Series CD1BA/3). 24 pages (cover announces 23 printed pages; last folio reads 24): English on every even index 2-22 (idx 2 = General Instructions), Hindi on every odd index 1-21 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked, all Hindi; idx 23 is blank (folio only). Q1-38 run unbroken across the even pages. Watermark bar down the left margin only; it covers no text. Instructions print 38 questions / 80 marks, Q1-18 MCQ, Q19-20 A-R, B 21-25 x2, C 26-31 x3, D 32-35 x5, E 36-38 x4: full80 confirmed. Instruction (viii) prints 2 internal choices in B, 2 in C, 2 in D and 3 in E: Q21, Q25, Q26, Q27, Q33, Q34, Q36(ii), Q37(ii), Q38(ii), all found on the paper with a printed OR and each reprinted with an OR in the marking scheme. No case study carries a printed 'Case Study - N' heading. Section-A keys read off the 30/3/3 marking scheme as images and each re-derived: all 20 agree. No void notes. Decimal points are ORDINARY full stops (Q2 0.045, Q11 7.5, Q38(ii)(b) 3.14). Sibling of 30/3/1: 42 rows are 30/3/1 questions (confirmed on this paper's pages, text reused byte-for-byte), 11 rows transcribed fresh (Q1, Q2, Q8, Q13, Q14, Q15, Q22, Q30, Q31, Q32, Q35); Q35 matches 2025 30/1/1 Q33(b) word for word and reuses that stem.

questions.context: Questions number 19 and 20 are Assertion and Reason based questions carrying 1 mark each. Two statements are given, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below :
questions.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The point which divides the line segment joining the points \(A(1, 2)\) and \(B(-1, 1)\) internally in the ratio 1 : 2 is \(\left(\dfrac{-1}{3}, \dfrac{5}{3}\right)\)

**Reason (R) :** The coordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining the points \(A(x_1, y_1)\) and \(B(x_2, y_2)\) in the ratio \(m_1 : m_2\) are \(\left(\dfrac{m_1x_2 + m_2x_1}{m_1 + m_2}, \dfrac{m_1y_2 + m_2y_1}{m_1 + m_2}\right)\)

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.stem: What is the lower limit of the modal class of the above data ?
